en:
I'm Nozomu Kazama.
A third-year.
This time, Hino talked me into it.
That Hino just wouldn't stop begging me.
He said a scary-story session can't do without me.
Honestly, I didn't really want to come.
Well, it can't be helped, right?
When someone asks me for something, I'm just not the type who can say no.
But I want you to take this one thing to heart.
Once you hear my story, all of you are going to be shocked.
Nobody else's story, no matter whose, can hold a candle to mine.
That's how incredible the secret I'm keeping is.
That's right.
So that Hino says I absolutely have to reveal my secret right here.
...I agonized over it.
Whether it was really all right to tell something like that here.
But now that I've come, there's no helping it.
I guess I'll reveal my best-kept secret.
...The truth is, I'm not human.{p}

Well? That surprised you, didn't it?
You see, I'm a different kind of being from all of you.
Whoa there, {c}{f:|}.
There's no need to be scared.
I'm not a bad guy, after all.{p}

Hey, {c}{f:|}.
What do you think I really am?
An alien
A subterranean
A being from another dimension
A yokai
An ordinary human
A nutcase
...That's right, I'm a nutcase...{f: like hell I am!| as if I am!}

Listen, okay?
I'll give you just one more chance.
If you give me another answer that makes no sense, I won't let you off lightly, got it?
Do you {f:understand|get} what 'won't let you off lightly' means?
{f:If you do, then|Anyway,} think about it seriously.{p}Now, look at me and tell me honestly what you think I really am.
An alien
A subterranean
A being from another dimension
A yokai
An ordinary human

...You've got pretty good instincts, haven't you?
Well, you've got me.
I was trying so hard to hide it, and you saw through me this easily.
Yep, I'm an alien.
{c}{f:|}, this is a big deal.
Right now, you're getting the biggest shock of your life.
After all, you're making contact with an extraterrestrial life form.{p}
Ask him to tell a story seriously
Ask him for proof that he's an alien
Get angry

"...Um, Kazama.
Excuse me, but we can't really make a newspaper out of that{f:,|,} so could you at least show us some proof that you're an alien?"
{f:I|I} worked up my nerve and said it.
Kazama seemed to think it over for a moment.{p}

"...So you don't believe me?
That I'm an alien?"
I believe you
I don't believe you
I can't say yet

I didn't believe him.
There was no way that could be true.
But I couldn't say that to his face, so for the moment I smoothed it over.
"...Um, it's not that I don't believe you.
It's just that hearing it from you alone isn't very convincing.
So I'd like you to show us some proof, even something simple, that will convince everyone."
Kazama jutted out his chin, apparently thinking something over.{p}

Then, slowly, he broke into a smirk.
Fine.
I get it.
In that case, I'll show you some proof.{p}

Could someone bring me a glass of water?
...Thank you.{p}

Put it on the table.
Yes, and then lay a sheet of thick paper on top of it.{p}
...And then, on top of that paper, right in the middle, I place a ten-yen coin.{p}

...Okay, you'd better watch closely.
Now, without touching this paper, I'm going to drop the ten-yen coin neatly into the glass.{p}Ready?
Wait a second. I can do that too
This looks kind of amazing. I'll watch quietly

"Ah, wait a second!
I can actually do that too..."{p}

"Hahaha... {a}.
You sure tell funny jokes.
This is something only a Sunbararian can do.
What could you possibly know about it?"
Kazama let out a loud, haughty laugh.
"...Um.
That wouldn't happen to be the trick where you set the paper on fire, the paper burns away, and the ten-yen coin drops in, would it..."{p}

Slowly, Kazama rose from his seat.
He seemed honestly astonished.
"...You knew!
...You're a sneaky one, aren't you?
So you're an alien too."{p}

With that, he suddenly broke into a friendly grin and clapped me on the shoulder.
What on earth is with this guy?{p}How do I answer?
Yes. I'm an alien too
No. I'm an Earthling

"No, I'm not.
{f:I|I}'m an Earthling.
I read about this in some quiz book."{p}Kazama wasn't taking what {f:I|I} said seriously.
"Oh, come on, quit joking around.
You're my comrade!"{p}

With that, he threw his arm around {f:my|my} shoulders.
Then he whispered softly in my ear.{p}
As {f:I|I} stared at Kazama in bewilderment, he nodded to himself and beamed.{p}

"Let's conquer the Earth together.
The preparations are complete."
Then he touched the thumb and index finger of his right hand together in an OK sign and winked at {f:me|me}.
...At that moment.
{f:I|I} didn't miss it.
Kazama's eyes glowed gold.
Kazama went back to his seat, looked around at everyone, and spoke.{p}

"Now, let's hear the next story.
We don't have much time, you see.
Something's come up that we need to talk over.
Who's going to tell the last story?"
With that, he looked at {f:me|me}, urging me on.
{f:We|We} don't have much time?
By '{f:we|we},' does he mean Kazama and {f:me|me}?
Talk over... what on earth is there to talk over{f:?|?}
...Anyway, that doesn't matter right now{f:.|.}
There are six people here, so unless a seventh shows up, the next story {f:will be|has to be} the last.
I {f:have to|have to} hear the last person's story...{p}

...Hm hm hm, looks like you've figured it out.
You've got sharp instincts, haven't you?
You've put me in a bind.
I work so hard to hide it, and it's no fun when it gets out this quickly.{p}

Yes, that's right.
I'm a subterranean.
My people are called the Bupekippo.
Remember that, okay?
By the way, {c}{f:|}, what did they teach you at school about what's at the bottom of the earth?
"Isn't it hot, seething magma?"
{f:I|I} said.{p}

"Tsk, tsk, it's not magma, dummy.
That's nothing but our camou-{g}flage.
And we borrow human form to blend in among you people.
You mustn't think you're the only living things on Earth.
Well? That was scary, wasn't it?
With this, your seven wonders paper is all set.
Lucky you, {c}{f:|}.
Now, shall we move on to the next person's story?"{p}

........Hey, wait.
What... that's the end?
Ending it {f:like this|like this} is {f:too much|just too much}.
{f:I|I} was an idiot to go along with a story like Kazama's{f:.|, wasn't I?}
There's no way this will make an article{f:.|.}{p}At this point, I need him to do something about it.
Ask him for proof that he's a subterranean
Ask him to tell a story seriously

"...Um, we can't really make a newspaper from that explanation, so could you show {f:us|us} some proof that you're a subterranean, Kazama?"
{f:I|I} worked up my nerve and said it.{p}

"If you're that suspicious, {f:girls are going to hate you|boys are going to be put off by you}.
So you don't trust me, is that it? You..."
I trust you
I don't trust you

"I can get by in daily life just fine like this, but I figured it would startle everyone."
And then he pushed the eyes back into the gaping holes.{p}

He pressed his ear to the floor.
Then he started muttering something to himself.{p}

"{f:Whoaaaaa|Eeeeeek}!
It's an {f:earthquake|earthquake}!"
I had to get under a desk, fast!
What on earth is {f:this|this}?{p}

"It's all right now."
When I came to my senses, the earthquake had already stopped.
Kazama was looking down at {f:us|us}, smiling.
"Do you all know what causes earthquakes?"
he asked.
Um, it was something to do with magma, I think...
Oh, {f:wait|wait}.
If what he'd been saying was true, then that {f:would be wrong|would be wrong, wouldn't it}.
"That's right. Every earthquake on Earth is controlled by us."
he said proudly.{p}

If what he said was true, this would make {f:huge|huge} news.
But... ordinary people would probably just say {f:I'd|I'd} lost my mind.
So that's why Kazama {f:gave off|gave off} a scent a little different from ordinary people.
I already knew he was no ordinary person, {f:though|though}.{p}

"{f:So|Um}, what business does a subterranean have up here on the surface?"
{f:I|I} asked.
"I'm a prince of the Underground Empire, you see.
They sent me up to the surface to learn a little about society.
Can't you sense the nobility just overflowing from me?"
he said boastfully.
Maybe {f:I|I} was dreaming...{p}

"Oh☆ Oh no!
It's snack time!"{p}

Kazama pulled some kind of jar out of his pocket.
"These are really tasty, you know."
With that, he calmly opened the lid and gulped the contents down in one go.
They were earthworms...
Worms that hadn't fit into his mouth yet were writhing and squirming slimily around his lips.
{f:I|I} thought...
You're not a mole! {f:Don't eat stuff like that|Please don't eat stuff like that}☆{p}

"Ahh, that was delicious☆
That's the end of my story, so next person, hurry up and start talking."
With that, Kazama smiled contentedly.
This {f:is|is} a bad dream.
...Anyway, none of that {f:matters|matters} right now.
There are six people here, so unless a seventh shows up, the next story will be the last.
I {f:have to|have to} hear the last person's story...{p}

...Hm hm hm, looks like you've figured it out.
You've got sharp instincts, haven't you?
You've put me in a bind.
I work so hard to hide it, and it's no fun when it gets out this quickly.
Yes, that's right.
I'm a being from another dimension, one who makes his home there.
Yes, we're called the Yapare.{p}

Just what have the Yapare come to the human world to do...?
{c}{f:|}, this is big news☆{p}

...So, that was scary, wasn't it?
With this, your seven wonders paper is all set.
Lucky you, {c}{f:|}.
Now, shall we move on to the next person's story?{p}

........Hey, wait.
What... that's the end?
Ending it {f:like this|like this} is {f:too much|just too much}.
{f:I|I} was an idiot to go along with a story like Kazama's{f:.|, wasn't I?}
There's no way this will make an article{f:.|.}{p}At this point, I need him to do something about it.
Ask him to tell a story seriously
Ask for proof he's from another dimension

"Please.
Tell it seriously.
We've been counting on your story, Kazama."
{f:I|I} begged him from the bottom of my heart.
But instead, Kazama started saying this.{p}

...You want me to tell it seriously?
This is no joke.
I'm perfectly serious.
We Yapare, who live in another dimension, have an advanced civilization.
From where we stand, you all look like you're living extremely primitive lives.
I'm one of an elite squad dispatched from another dimension.
Why were we sent, you ask?{p}

We found out that the planet in our dimension, the one we lived on, doesn't have long left.
Even with all the science of our civilization, there's no avoiding it.
So we've been searching for a new place to move to.
Other comrades of ours are scouting around for places we could settle, too, but it isn't going well.
Well, for now, Earth is the top candidate for our move.{p}

Oh, you don't need to worry.
We take good care of the natives.
Yes, we're a pitiful race.{p}Don't you think so?
Pitiful
This guy is weird

"How {f:pitiful|pitiful}, Kazama..."
{f:I|I} said.
Though really, I meant it in a different way.
"...Thank you. How kind Earthlings are.
I'm deeply moved.
{c}{f:|}, thank you for your sympathy.
Looks like we'll get along fine with you all from now on. Wonderful, wonderful.
Oh, I know☆"{p}

With that, Kazama stood by the window.
Then he raised his hand toward the {f:sky|sky}.{p}

Then the sky split wide open, and a dazzling beam of light shone down from the gap.
{f:I|I} was bathed in that light.{p}

{f:I|I} somehow felt warm inside, as if my heart had been washed {f:clean|clean}.
Kazama said,
"Looks like you've received the message from our representative.
Well, now that that's settled, there are no more problems between us.
Now that we're all feeling happy, shall we hear the next person's story?"
...But {f:I'm|I'm} just an ordinary citizen.
I think he'd do better telling that sort of thing to someone far more important than {f:me|me}.
Oh well, {f:whatever|whatever}, at this point...{p}
Actually, you probably don't know this, but all sorts of yokai are hiding in this human world in disguise.{p}

By the way, {c}{f:|}, does your family keep a dog?
Hmm, you do?
What's its name?
It's called Pohe... What a cute name.
Well, even Pohe might not really be a dog.
From what I've seen, thirty percent of the dogs in the human world are a yokai called a sunekosuri.
It's true.
Me?
I'm a yokai called a nurarihyon.
We don't do anything bad.
There are evil yokai too, though.
You know the people who get arrested for violent crimes? Most of them are evil yokai.{p}

...So, that was scary, wasn't it?
With this, your seven wonders paper is all set.
Lucky you, {c}{f:|}.
Now, shall we move on to the next person's story?{p}

........Hey, wait.
What... that's the end?
Ending it {f:like this|like this} is {f:too much|just too much}.
{f:I|I} was an idiot to go along with a story like Kazama's{f:.|, wasn't I?}
There's no way this will make an article{f:.|.}{p}At this point, I need him to do something about it.
Ask for proof he's a yokai
Ask him to tell a story seriously

"...Um, I don't think we can really make a paper out of that explanation, so could you show {f:us|us} some proof that you're a yokai, Kazama?"
{f:I|I} took the plunge and asked.{p}
"If you're that suspicious, {f:girls are going to hate you|boys are going to be put off by you}.{p}So you don't trust me, is that it? You..."
I trust you
I don't trust you

"No, no, it's not that I don't trust you, Kazama.
{f:I|I} trust you completely, Kazama.
Yes, I absolutely trust you☆"
{f:I|I} was getting all worked up.
I could {f:never|never} say something like that unless I just blurted it out.{p}

"Thank you, {c}{f:|}.
I'm so happy.
I was worried that even if I told my secret, nobody would believe me.
Those words of yours were just what I wanted to hear.
Still, it'll probably make your article easier to write if I show you proof right here that I'm a yokai."{p}

With that, he walked over to {f:me|me}.
"All right, {c}{f:|}, close your eyes.
Don't open them until I say so."
{f:I|I} closed my eyes as Kazama told me.{p}

...................................What's {f:going on|going on}?
Nothing's happening at {f:all|all}.{p}Just how long am I supposed to stay like {f:this|this}?
Can't stand it, open my eyes
Hold out
{f:I|I} couldn't stand it any longer and opened my eyes.{p}

...He was picking his nose.
"K-Kazama?"
{f:I|I} said, dumbfounded.
He spoke, looking a little put out.{p}

"Ah, I told you not to open your eyes, didn't I?
You have to keep your promises.
If you can't keep a promise, I can't show you the proof."
And {f:I|I} didn't miss the words he muttered under his breath next.
"And here I was, thinking up proof that I'm a yokai while you had your eyes closed..."
...Hey☆
Proof isn't something you think {f:up|up}!
There's a limit to how far you can mess with {f:people|people}!
Grrrrrrrrrr☆
...........No.
It was {f:my|my} own fault for going along with a guy like {f:Kazama|Kazama}.
{f:Right|Right}, I'd known that perfectly well from the very start.
Ugh, {f:I'm|I'm} such an {f:idiot|idiot}.
Then, eyeing {f:me|me} sidelong, Kazama said this.
"{c}{f:, since you spoiled it all|, since you broke your promise}, my story ends here.
Well, too bad, but let's hear the next person's story."{p}
Heh, thank you.

I blend in with humans so perfectly, it's only natural you couldn't tell.
Sorry for asking you something so strange...{p}
The truth is, I'm really not human.{p}So what do you think I really am?
An alien
A subterranean
A being from another dimension
A yokai

"Serious?
{f:How rude|That's mean}. Are you calling me a liar?
I'm perfectly serious.
I'll have you know, I pride myself on being the most honest person there is.
I can't accept being branded a liar like that{f:.|!}
{f:Huh|Well}?"
He {f:said, a little offended|got a little offended}.
"...So basically, you don't trust me.
Is what I told you really that hard to believe?"{p}

Humans always get worked up like that over things they can't understand."
Kazama took {f:my|my} outburst more calmly than I'd expected.
{f:I|I} suddenly felt embarrassed about raising my voice.
"Kazama...
I'm sorry about earlier.
Yelling like that...
I just..."
{f:I|I} apologized to him.
Then I went on.
"...Um, if you could show us some proof that you're an alien, even something simple..."
Kazama glanced at {f:me|me} and said,{p}

...You're {f:a hopeless guy|a naughty girl}, aren't you?
You should take what people say at face value.
Oh, wait, I'm not a person, am I?
That's right, I'm an alien.
Ha ha ha ha ha.
...Oops, excuse me.
I got off track.
You want to see proof that I'm an alien, right?
Okay, got it.{p}

"...I never said I didn't trust you, Kazama.
If you say so, Kazama, then {f:we|we} believe you.
Yes☆
Even if everyone else refuses to believe you, {f:I|I} alone will believe you☆
Kazama☆
Huff, huff, huff..."
{f:I|I} found myself getting all worked up.
If I didn't say something like that for now, who knew what he'd say to me {f:later|later}.
He calmly soothed {f:me|me} and went on with his story.{p}

...Now, now, {c}{f:|}, no need to get so worked up about it.
You're shaken because I came out with that so suddenly, right?
All right, then I'll show you proof that I'm an alien.
That should convince everyone, I think...{p}

Precisely because he was strange enough to say this sort of thing without batting an eye, I couldn't tell what the truth really was.
{f:Yes|Yes}, maybe what he said was true.
{f:No|No}, {f:but|but}...
{f:I|I} considered myself a person with common sense, and yet.
What was I supposed to do with this contradiction...?
Maybe it was precisely because it was Kazama that I felt I still couldn't say either way.
{f:But|But} what criteria did Hino use to pick Kazama...?
There was no point thinking about that right {f:now|now}...
"Well then, for now, if you could show us proof that you're an alien, Kazama..."
Kazama smiled gently and said,{p}

Then Kazama held his hand over the glass.
"Hmmmmmmmmmm, hnnnnnnnngh..."
With his eyes closed, Kazama {f:seemed|seemed} to be sending some kind of psychic energy into the glass.
......................................Nothing's happening, though.
{f:I|I} glanced at my watch.
Five minutes had already gone by.
Unable to hold back, {f:I|I} whispered to Kazama.
"Um, are we going to be waiting much longer?"
Kazama popped one eye open and looked at {f:me|me}.{p}

"It's no good, I seem to be off my game today.
I'm sorry, I've let everyone down!
Forgive me..."
Kazama bowed his head to {f:me|me}.{p}

Just then, one of the people watching smiled, picked up the ten-yen coin, lifted the paper, and gently dropped the coin into the glass.
Then, deliberately,

"Th-the ten-yen coin is in the glass☆"
they {f:said|said}.{p}

Kazama turned around.
"...See!
Just like I said, right?
That's my alien power for you, in a nutshell!
Thank you all for your cooperation!
Thank youuu☆"
Everyone was holding back laughter.
At least now we could move on to the next story without putting him in a bad {f:mood|mood}.
As for {f:me|me}, the moment the paper, the glass and the ten-yen coin came out,
(Ugh, this might be a lost cause...)
was what I'd {f:thought, honestly|thought, honestly}.
At first, I'd thought I had to somehow turn Kazama's story into an article.
But I'd had enough of his {f:story|story}...
"Ahem, so, now that it's been proven that Kazama is an alien, may we have the next person's story, please?"{p}

"I won't press you on where you learned about the Sunbararians' special powers.
But... it seems you're from some other planet.
You smell different. Your smell..."
Kazama said.{p}
Then Kazama whispered in {f:my|my} ear.{p}
"☆☆★·☆··☆"{p}Now, how should I react?
Brush him off with any old answer
Tell him to quit fooling around
Without thinking, {f:I|I} just said whatever came out,

"☆··★☆·☆"
That was my answer.
What a pushover {f:I|I} {f:am|am}.
Now that I think about it, I'm doing something really stupid.
But Kazama... {f:he didn't have to go that far|he didn't have to go that far}.
He's obsessive about the weirdest things, or {f:maybe he's just plain dumb|it's all just plain silly}...{p}

Then I noticed Kazama suddenly looked angry.
"We offered to conquer this planet together with you people!
And you're turning us down?★"
Wh-what are {f:you|you} saying, Kazama?
{f:I|I} only gave him a random answer.
"We Sunbararians basically don't get emotional, but if that's how you want it, we've got plans of our own!
Damn you, Pohipohian!"
{f:M|M}-{f:me|me}, a Pohipohian?{p}

Ignoring {f:me|me} as I stood there dumbfounded, Kazama went to the window.
Then he raised his hand toward the sky.
"Reporting!
On Earth, we have discovered aliens besides ourselves who seek to conquer it!
They have trampled on our goodwill.
Commence the Earth invasion plan at once☆"{p}

At that moment, two balls of light suddenly appeared in the sky.
Those are flying saucers★
No, that's crazy...
Then the two balls of light fired beams at each other and burst into a blinding glare.{p}

"{f:Whoa|Eek}☆"
{f:I|I} instinctively looked away.{p}

Wh-{f:what|what}... what on earth {f:was|was} that☆
There was nothing but empty sky stretching out {f:there|there}.{p}

Kazama spoke to {f:me|me}, looking disappointed.
"The Sunbararian and Pohipohian ships shot each other down and were destroyed...
You'll pay for this, Pohipohian!
Next time, you won't get off so easy!"
...At that moment...
{f:I|I} didn't miss it.
Kazama's eyes glowed gold.
Kazama went back to his seat, looked around at everyone, and spoke.{p}

"Serious?
{f:How rude|That's mean}. Are you calling me a liar?
I'm perfectly serious.
I'll have you know, I pride myself on being the most honest person there is.
I can't accept being branded a liar like that{f:.|.}
{f:Huh|Well}?"
He said it a little sulkily.{p}

"...So basically, you don't trust me.
Is what I told you really that hard to believe?"{p}He looked displeased{f:.|.}

"I trust you, Kazama!
If you say so, Kazama, then {f:we|we} believe you.
Yes☆
Even if everyone else refuses to believe you, {f:I|I} alone will believe you☆ Kazama☆
Huff, huff, huff..."
{f:I|I} found myself getting all worked up.
If I didn't say something like that for now, who knew what he'd say to me later{f:.|.}
"It's all right, you don't have to force yourself.
I'll show you the proof, nice and thoroughly..."
Kazama said with a broad smile.{p}

"I can get by in daily life just fine like this, but I figured it would startle everyone."
And then he pushed the eyes back into the gaping holes.{p}

"We can communicate with each other through ultrasound."
He twitched his ears.
Apparently he could move them however he liked.
Th-that's {f:amazing|amazing}.
{f:With|With} that, it {f:makes sense|makes sense} that he doesn't need eyes.
"Do you all know how earthquakes happen?"
He asked {f:me|me}.
"Um, it's something to do with magma, right..."
{f:I|I} started to say, but he cut me off.
"Tsk, tsk, tsk. We're the ones who control all of them."
Kazama said that and held up his index finger.
"And I can do things like this, too."{p}

He pressed his ear to the floor.
Then he {f:seemed to be muttering|started muttering} something to himself.{p}

"...Oh, cr-crap☆"
Kazama said, flustered.{p}

"Kazama, this is no time for 'what do I do'!
{f:Gyaaaaaaah|Nooooooo}☆"{p}

{f:I|I} watched the pillar behind me crumble down, unable to even move...
No way {f:I|I}'m dying because some subterranean messed up! That's too stupid!{p}

"You want me to show you proof?"
Kazama stroked his chin for a while, then said:
"You see, I've been acting strictly as a human to avoid causing a panic.
So whatever happens here, you mustn't tell a soul.
Got it? Understood?"
With that, he traced a circle in the air with his finger.{p}

Then, where his finger had traced the circle, a black hole gaped open.
Inside it, bands of all kinds of light swirled against the black.
"This is where we live."
With that, he stuck his face into the hole and clowned around.
Then he closed the black hole with his fingers and spoke.{p}

...We Yapare, who live in another dimension, have an advanced civilization.
From where we stand, you people seem to live extremely primitive lives.
I'm one of an elite unit dispatched from the other dimension.
Why was I dispatched, you ask?{p}

The planet we lived on in the other dimension was attacked by the Hidebu, a savage interdimensional race.
Thanks to them, we were forced to flee in escape ships.
We're not a warlike race, you see.
We don't like violent fights.
So we thought, why not just move somewhere else altogether...
